name: arc-diagonal-then-straight-path
description: Use when ARC grids show isolated 1 and 2 markers; connect them with a 3 path that is diagonal first, then straight, ending diagonally adjacent to 2.
---

# ARC diagonal-then-straight connector

Use for the observed ARC pattern where a lone color-1 marker and a lone color-2 marker sit on an otherwise blank grid, and the output adds color 3 between them.

## Rule inferred from demos

Starting from the color-1 cell, move in the signs of the row and column differences toward color 2, drawing a 45-degree diagonal segment, then continue along the remaining axis in a straight line. Stop at the cell diagonally adjacent to 2 (one row and one column away), rather than overwriting either marker. Leave all other cells unchanged.

For 0-based coordinates `start=(r1,c1)`, `target=(r2,c2)`:
- `dr = sign(r2-r1)`, `dc = sign(c2-c1)`.
- Draw diagonal 3s at `(r1+k*dr, c1+k*dc)` for `k=1..min(abs(r2-r1),abs(c2-c1))-1`.
- From the last diagonal cell, continue with 3s along the axis with the larger absolute displacement until reaching `(r2-dr, c2-dc)`, which is diagonally adjacent to the target.
- Retain the original 1 and 2 cells.

This yields a path that terminates one step diagonally from 2. E.g. one demo had 1 at (10,1), 2 at (3,11), with diagonal cells through (4,7), then horizontal 3s to (4,10). The successfully solved test had 1 at (1,4), 2 at (13,12), diagonal cells through (8,11), then vertical 3s ending at (12,11).

## Caution

Only one demonstration and one confirmed test instance establish this behavior. Check whether the markers are otherwise isolated and whether the demonstrated geometry matches before applying; degenerate cases (same row/column, adjacent markers, equal offsets) are not verified. This path is diagonal followed by straight, not a conventional shortest grid path and not a full diagonal all the way to 2.",
